full_article:
Nepal’s digital government overhaul is facing mounting failures as demand outstrips capacity and critical national platforms buckle under structural constraints.

Failures in strategic and systemic planning have led to acute problems, argues an in-depth report in The Kathmandu Post. Nepal’s national identity infrastructure has seen extensive technical failures over the past weeks, leaving thousands unable to access services that are verified through the National Identity Management Information System (NIDMIS).

IN Groupe supplied both NIDMIS and Nepal’s Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS), and has deployed specialists to Kathmandu.

The central National Identity Card (NID) verification network along with land and property registration databases, transport management portals, immigration systems and tax platforms have all suffered major outages in recent months. These disruptions have stalled public services, halted transactions and, in some cases, shut down departments for weeks.

Reportedly, the problems stem from outdated hardware, flawed procurement, dependence on foreign vendors and a shortage of specialized technical staff. The past decade has seen dozens of digital platforms, which range from budgeting and treasury systems, to tax management tools and citizen apps. However, there is a lack of infrastructure, interoperability or technical capacity needed to sustain them.

The National ID database suffers arguably the severest strain. As more agencies make NID verification mandatory, it’s become a single point of failure. The services modern societies depend on — banks, telecoms, transport offices and the passport department — all route verification requests to the central server. According to reports, the system’s biometric‑matching engine has reached saturation.

Experts say high‑traffic services were connected to the NID server without expanding processing power or storage. During peak hours, thousands of simultaneous verification requests overwhelm the system, causing delays or complete lockouts. Older government platforms use XML‑based APIs, reportedly, while newer ones use REST, requiring translation layers that slow performance and destabilize systems.

E‑governance specialists say a procurement culture, one that is supposedly geared toward acquiring systems, has resulted in a dearth of longer-term thinking. Agencies spend months on tenders but often fail to secure service level agreements, uptime guarantees or maintenance plans. There appears to be a layer of accounting missing as expected users, peak traffic, storage and security, are frequently overlooked, and projects launch without feasibility studies or capacity forecasts.

Changes to sustain the system

Nepal’s digital recovery will require structural fixes, insiders and experts say. This begins with a shift away from siloed servers in individual ministries and toward a unified national cloud architecture. A modern cloud backbone would let the state scale computing power as demand rises, distribute workloads more evenly and maintain redundant failover systems. This means traffic spikes would be less likely to crash essential services.

Another point of contention is Nepal’s reliance on proprietary foreign systems. Adopting open‑standard architectures could give local engineers more autonomy and control over integration, upgrades and troubleshooting.

Core biometric or cryptographic engines may still need global vendors, but the surrounding layers, including citizen‑facing interfaces, middleware, API connectors and secondary modules, could be built domestically on open frameworks such as MOSIP. The open-source foundation helps countries build secure, sovereign and interoperable digital public goods like digital identity. The platform supports a global ecosystem of governments, implementation partners, technology providers and standards — Biometric Update has a 47-page report on MOSIP.

The Public Procurement Act should be updated, experts say, to reflect the full lifecycle of software. Meanwhile, offering competitive salaries to attract and retain skilled IT professionals, mandating regular technical audits, and performance reviews of government databases, will strengthen Nepal’s digital foundations.

title: Nepal Recovers Five Bodies of Climbers From Last Fall - Explorersweb »
description: Nepal Recovers Five Bodies of Climbers From Last Fall  Explorersweb »
publisher.title: Explorersweb »
full_article:
Searchers have finally retrieved five bodies from the slopes of Yalung Ri, a 5,630m trekking peak in Nepal, after an avalanche buried them on November 3, 2025.

Locals spotted the bodies near the base of the mountain in Rolwaling last week and called authorities. Despite the monsoon, warm summer temperatures had melted the snow under which they had been buried.

Bad weather thwarted a first attempt to send a helicopter with a recovery team, but a second attempt last Sunday succeeded, The Kathmandu Post reported. However, searchers needed seven attempts to get the bodies off the mountain in quickly worsening weather and hazardous conditions. The helicopter only managed to transport them to the nearby Na village that evening, and then resumed the flight to Kathmandu on Monday.

File image of climbers on a snow-loaded Yalung Ri. Photo: All Nepal Hiking

Seven victims in all

The deceased climbers are Padang Tamang and Mer Karki, both of Nepal, and Marco Di Marcello of Canada, Markus Kerchler of Italy, and Jakob Schreiber of Germany.

They were five of the seven victims of a deadly avalanche that hit as they climbed the mountain last fall. The two others were retrieved from the mountain during the initial rescue. Four other climbers were also injured.

Some of the victims were acclimatizing on Yalung Ri before climbing the higher Dolma Khang. Others were apparently trekkers on the peak, which is below 6,000m and so only requires a trekking permit.

Avalanche-swept terrain on Yalung Ri in November, 2025. Photo: The Tourism Times

The 2025 disaster

The circumstances of that accident were never detailed. Cyclone Montha had wrapped Nepal’s mountains in heavy snow for more than five days, likely creating unstable or excessive snow on the slopes. In addition, there was another deadly avalanche in Nepal that week: Two Italian climbers died in an avalanche that hit them when they were in Camp 1 on Pambari, a 6,887m peak northwest of Manaslu.

A two-day delay in aerial assistance after the accident due to administrative hurdles made the case particularly controversial.

“The emergency response was immediately snared in red tape because the Rolwaling Valley is designated a restricted zone, requiring multiple layers of permission for rescue flights,” The Tourism Times reported at the time. Injured climbers had to wait a further 24 hours to be airlifted to the hospital.

French long-distance hiker Carole Fuchs was in the area doing the 1,700km Great Himalaya Trail and helped an injured climber as much as she could. In a later report, she described the “red-tape nightmare” she went through to get help. IFMGA guide Mingma G, a native of Rolwaling, wrote bluntly, “The seven climbers were killed by the government, not the avalanche.”

View this post on Instagram See this post on Instagram

Easy does not mean safe

Yalung Ri is a straightforward peak, but the normal snowy route passes under a potentially dangerous serac. In addition, slab avalanches are possible, as the upper part of the climb goes up steep ramps of snow and ice.

title: Remains of Three Elite Nepali Climbers Repatriated After Deadly Broad Peak Avalanche - ABC NEWS NEPAL
description: Remains of Three Elite Nepali Climbers Repatriated After Deadly Broad Peak Avalanche  ABC NEWS NEPAL
publisher.title: ABC NEWS NEPAL
full_article:
Kathmandu— The remains of three highly accomplished Nepali climbers – Kili Pemba Sherpa, Gyalu Sherpa, and Nima Sherpa – were returned to Nepal on Tuesday, bringing to a close one chapter in the aftermath of the devastating July 30 avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan’s Karakoram range. The bodies arrived at Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport aboard a Qatar Airways flight from Doha, where they were met by grieving relatives, fellow climbers, and officials from the Nepal Mountaineering Association and expedition companies. The three Sherpas were among ten climbers killed when an avalanche struck between Camp 2 and Camp 3 on the 8,051-meter peak.

A Nation Mourns

Emotions ran high at Tribhuvan International Airport as officials unloaded the coffins from the aircraft. Family members broke down in tears beside the caskets during airport formalities before the bodies were transported to their respective destinations. The loss of these experienced guides represents a significant blow to Nepal’s climbing community and highlights the inherent risks faced by those who support expeditions on the world's highest peaks.

Distinguished Climbing Careers

Kili Pemba Sherpa, 46, was renowned for his extensive experience, including participation in the first winter ascent of K2 in January 2021 and a recent completion of all fourteen 8,000-meter peaks with a summit of Nanga Parbat. He worked as a guide for Imagine Nepal. Gyalu Sherpa, also known as Gyaljen, hailed from Okhaldhunga and had summited Kanchenjunga three times in a single season – a record considered exceptional by many climbers – alongside numerous ascents of Mount Everest. Nima Sherpa, in his mid-30s, was a senior guide for Elite Exped and had already summited four 8,000-meter peaks during the 2026 season before embarking on the ill-fated Broad Peak expedition.

Ongoing Recovery Efforts

The bodies of Pur Bahadur Gurung and British-Nepali climber Nirmal Purja have also been repatriated; Purja’s remains were flown to the United Kingdom, where he held citizenship. However, recovery efforts are ongoing for three climbers – one Nepali, one Pakistani, and one American – who remain on the mountain, hampered by challenging high-altitude conditions. Broad Peak, located on the border of Pakistan and China, is known as a technically demanding but less crowded 8,000-meter peak compared to nearby K2.

Mountaineering Risks and Changing Conditions

The avalanche that struck Broad Peak has been described by veteran climbers as one of the deadliest single incidents in the mountain’s history. The exposed sections between Camp 2 and Camp 3 have previously experienced avalanche activity, and mountaineers have noted increasingly unpredictable snowpack conditions in the Karakoram range. Some experts attribute these changing patterns to shifting weather systems that are making route assessment more difficult.

The July 30th disaster is considered one of the worst tragedies affecting Nepali high-altitude workers since the 2014 Everest icefall avalanche and the 2015 earthquake-triggered avalanche at Everest Base Camp.

(With inputs from ANI)

एक राष्ट्र शोक

त्रिभुवन अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डा पर अधिकारी सब विमान स चिता उतारला पर भावुकता तेज भ गेल। हवाई अड्डा के औपचारिकता के दौरान लाश के अपन-अपन गंतव्य तक पहुंचाबय सं पहिने परिवार के लोक कास्केट के बगल मे नोर सं टूटि गेल. ई अनुभवी गाइड केरऽ नुकसान नेपाल केरऽ पर्वतारोही समुदाय लेली एगो महत्वपूर्ण झटका के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै आरू दुनिया केरऽ सबसें ऊँचऽ चोटी प॑ अभियान के समर्थन करै वाला लोगऽ के सामने आबै वाला अंतर्निहित जोखिमऽ प॑ प्रकाश डालै छै ।

विशिष्ट पर्वतारोहण करियर

46 वर्षीय किली पेम्बा शेर्पा अपनऽ व्यापक अनुभव लेली प्रसिद्ध छेलै, जेकरा म॑ जनवरी २०२१ म॑ के२ केरऽ पहलऽ शीतकालीन चढ़ाई म॑ भागीदारी आरू हाल ही म॑ नांगा पर्बत केरऽ शिखर के साथ ८,००० मीटर केरऽ सब चौदह चोटी पूरा होय के काम शामिल छेलै । इमेजिन नेपाल के लेल गाइड के काज केलनि। ग्यालु शेर्पा, जेकरा ग्यालजेन के नाम स॑ भी जानलऽ जाय छै, ओखलढुंगा के रहै वाला छेलै आरू एक सीजन म॑ तीन बार कंचनजुंगा के शिखर पर पहुँची चुकलऽ छेलै – जेकरा बहुत पर्वतारोही द्वारा असाधारण मानलऽ जाय छै – माउंट एवरेस्ट केरऽ अनेक चढ़ाई के साथ-साथ । ३० के दशक के मध्य में निमा शेर्पा एलिट एक्सपेड के सीनियर गाइड छेली आरू २०२६ के सीजन के दौरान ८,००० मीटर के चार चोटी के शिखर पर चढ़ी चुकलऽ छेलै, जेकरा बाद वू दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण ब्रॉड पीक अभियान में निकली चुकलऽ छेलै ।

चल रहे वसूली के प्रयास

पुर बहादुर गुरुंग आ अंग्रेज-नेपाली पर्वतारोही निर्मल पुर्जा केर शव सेहो वापस आबि गेल अछि; पुरजा केरऽ पार्थिव शरीर क॑ उड़ान भरलऽ गेलै यूनाइटेड किंगडम, जहां हुनका नागरिकता छेलै । लेकिन, तीन पर्वतारोही – एक नेपाली, एक पाकिस्तानी, आरू एक अमेरिकी – के वसूली के प्रयास जारी छै, जे चुनौतीपूर्ण उच्च ऊंचाई के परिस्थिति के कारण बाधित पहाड़ पर बनलऽ छै । पाकिस्तान आरू चीन के सीमा प॑ स्थित ब्रॉड पीक क॑ तकनीकी रूप स॑ मांग वाला लेकिन नजदीकी के२ के तुलना म॑ कम भीड़ वाला ८,००० मीटर के चोटी के रूप म॑ जानलऽ जाय छै ।

पर्वतारोहण के जोखिम आ बदलैत परिस्थिति

ब्रॉड पीक पर आयल हिमस्खलन के अनुभवी पर्वतारोही सब एहि पहाड़ के इतिहास के सबस घातक एकल घटना में सं एक बतौने छथि. कैम्प २ आरू कैम्प ३ के बीच के उजागर खंडऽ म॑ पहल॑ ही हिमस्खलन गतिविधि के अनुभव होय चुकलऽ छै, आरू पर्वतारोही न॑ काराकोरम श्रृंखला म॑ तेजी स॑ अप्रत्याशित बर्फ के पैक केरऽ स्थिति नोट करलकै । किछु विशेषज्ञ एहि बदलैत पैटर्न कए बदलैत मौसम प्रणाली कए मानैत छथि जे मार्ग क आकलन कए आओर कठिन बना रहल अछि ।

title: Balen Shah, India-Nepal Relations and the Road to Economic Statecraft - Daily Pioneer
description: Balen Shah, India-Nepal Relations and the Road to Economic Statecraft  Daily Pioneer
publisher.title: Daily Pioneer
full_article:
As Balen Shah begins engaging India, China and others, the larger test will be whether this diplomatic space can be translated into strategic economic opportunities — particularly through deeper India-Nepal value-chain integration and access to global markets

A compliment is certainly due to newly elected Prime Minister Balendra Shah for taking time to find his feet before engaging Nepal's key partners. He has demonstrated resilience and composure amid relentless social-media berating over what many described as his "strategic silence." Perhaps, in the process, PM Shah stole all the gossip!

Setting aside the pun, all eyes are now on Monday, August 10, when Prime Minister Shah is expected to meet the Indian and Chinese envoys, followed by the US Chargé d'affaires on Tuesday, as reported by The Kathmandu Post.

This appears to be a carefully sequenced set of engagements with Nepal's two vital neighbours.

India remains strategically vital to Nepal for trade, commerce, connectivity and extensive people-to-people linkages. Nepal's historic linkages with China likewise extend beyond contemporary geopolitics, including important economic, cultural and people-to-people exchanges with the Tibet Autonomous Region, particularly across Nepal's northern region.

Interestingly, The Kathmandu Post has reported that Prime Minister Shah did not receive requests for meetings with US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs Samir Paul Kapur and President Donald Trump's Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor, and subsequently did not grant an audience to US Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy Sarah B. Rogers. I do not have details of these requests or the circumstances surrounding the reported decisions. It would therefore be inappropriate to draw definitive conclusions about the Prime Minister's intent. But the reported sequence deserves more than passing diplomatic commentary. The issue is not whether Nepal should engage the United States. Of course it should. Nor is declining a meeting, by itself, evidence of hostility.

The larger question is whether the expectations, approach or conduct of some external actors adequately recognise Nepal's sovereign diplomatic space. Nepal is a sovereign state pursuing a delicate foreign policy between its two immediate neighbours, India and China, while maintaining relations with the United States and other international partners. Its leadership has every right to determine whom it meets, when it meets and at what level. Nepal may be a smaller state in economic and military terms, but its geopolitical significance far exceeds its size. Situated between two major Asian powers, it is strategically important not only to its neighbours but also to global powers.

That makes sensitivity and calibration essential. Diplomatic presence should not become an end in itself, nor should access to a sovereign government be treated as an entitlement. Nepal is not closing its doors. It is engaging. But the reported sequencing could indicate that engagement must take place on the basis of sovereign choice, reciprocity and diplomatic respect.

For policymakers in Washington, Kathmandu and beyond, the more important question is not simply, "Why did Nepal decline the meeting?", a question to which I do not have the answer but: What can observers learn from this reported pattern of engagement, and what does it tell us about the assumptions, expectations and methods of external diplomatic engagement in Nepal?

For a newly elected Prime Minister, taking time to understand the lay of the land, domestically, regionally and geopolitically before opening the diplomatic calendar may not be hesitation. It may simply be statecraft.

If this is the beginning, Nepal's young leadership has certainly made a noteworthy start. From Sovereign Agency to Economic Statecraft: What Next for Nepal-India Relations?

Sovereign agency, however, is not an end in itself. The real test of statecraft is what Nepal does with it. This is where the next conversation should begin with economic diplomacy and, more importantly, economic statecraft.

The impetus being given by Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to economic diplomacy is welcome. Its engagement with government, business, chambers, investors and other stakeholders recognises an important reality: economic diplomacy cannot remain confined to the Foreign Ministry or diplomatic corps. It must translate diplomatic relationships into measurable economic opportunities.

For India-Nepal relations, this could be transformational. The conversation should move beyond trade figures and aid narratives towards value chains, investment, manufacturing, services, energy, tourism, digital connectivity, logistics and market access.

As Prime Minister Balendra Shah's engagement with India takes shape, one strategic question ought to be placed squarely on the table:

How can Nepal leverage India's network of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (CEPAs) with third countries to expand Nepal's own exports, attract investment, strengthen manufacturing and integrate into regional and global value chains? This is precisely the kind of question Nepal's Chambers of Commerce should be asking and developing into a concrete economic strategy. To date, however, I have not seen a dedicated chamber-led study going sufficiently deep into this opportunity.

Nor is this opportunity merely for Nepal. India's Chambers of Commerce should equally examine how India's growing network of FTAs and CEPAs can give regional economic integration a strategic boost. India has built what could be described as a treasure trove of market-access arrangements. The question now is how these agreements can become more than instruments for bilateral trade and provide a platform for regional value-chain integration.

Nepal should therefore ask: Where can Nepal add value? Where can Indian investment create manufacturing capacity in Nepal? Which products can enter Indian and regional supply chains? Which sectors can jointly target FTA/CEPA markets? And what rules of origin, standards, connectivity and policy arrangements would make this commercially viable? This is where economic diplomacy must move beyond trade statistics and Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) to strategic value-chain thinking. The opportunity could extend across hydropower and clean energy, agro-processing, tea and coffee, herbs and essential oils, textiles, tourism, IT and digital services, pharmaceuticals, light manufacturing and logistics.

For India, deeper value chain integration in above-mentioned areas with Nepal could strengthen the economic architecture of the neighbourhood while creating additional production and supply-chain capabilities for accessing third-country markets.

It is time to reframe the question from:

"How much does Nepal export to India?"

to: "How can India and Nepal together create value in Nepal, integrate that value into Indian supply chains, and leverage India's global market access?" That is the conversation I would like to see begin with Prime Minister Shah and Ambassador Srivastava, and, equally importantly, with the Chambers of Commerce on both sides. For Nepal, sovereignty is not simply the ability to choose whom to meet. It is also the ability to define what it seeks from those relationships. The next test of Nepal's young leadership is to convert sovereign agency into strategic economic opportunity.

The larger question is whether the expectations, approach or conduct of some external actors adequately recognise Nepal's sovereign diplomatic space. title: El Niño yet to make an impact on monsoon - The Rising Nepal
description: El Niño yet to make an impact on monsoon  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug. 12: The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM), in its 2026 monsoon outlook, forecast below-normal rainfall in parts of southern and western Nepal, particularly southern Karnali, Lumbini, eastern Madhes and southern Koshi. The outlook also highlighted the potential influence of the El Niño conditions developing in the Pacific Ocean on the country’s monsoon pattern.

However, seeing the situation until mid-monsoon, the country received 92.1 per cent (611.5 mm) of the rainfall until August 6, which is slightly below but not so low which was projected in the outlook, experts said.

According to DHM, the nation received an average cumulative precipitation of 611.5 mm, standing at 92.1 per cent of its historical average (1991 to 2026) of 663.6 mm for this time frame (June 19 to August 6).

Madhes Province recorded the lowest relative precipitation nationwide, receiving just 81.9 per cent of its normal rainfall during this period. Similarly, the Tarai belt of Koshi Province saw significant deficits, operating at only 76 per cent of standard seasonal precipitation.

In contrast, central and western regions have experienced near-normal monsoon patterns. Sudurpaschim Province and Karnali Province stood closest to historical averages, recording 98.6 per cent and 97.5 per cent of normal precipitation, respectively.

Bagmati Province, which includes the Kathmandu Valley, logged 93.8 per cent of its normal rainfall. Kathmandu Airport measured 773.5 mm of rain during the period, exceeding its seasonal benchmark of 565.1 mm.

Despite the nationwide shortfall, localized downpours have caused heavy precipitation in select hilly and mountainous pockets. Stations such as Num in Koshi Province recorded 1,567 mm of rainfall, while Malepatan in Pokhara registered 1,379.2 mm.

Overall, rainfall has remained fairly consistent across the country, although it is slightly below normal. Heavy rainfall has been recorded in a few areas, according to DHM.

Ngmindra Dahal, a climate analyst, said El Niño is something related to temperature. When the temperature changes, it affects moisture, the water vapour and wind patterns. So, the primary factor is temperature, which is historically at an extremely high level right now. The impacts it has on atmospheric systems and the growth of moisture are also occurring, but those are secondary effects. The tertiary impact is the effect it has on our existing monsoon cycle. That is the third level of impact, he informed.

The DHM has been saying that rainfall would be well below average. “We are not hearing as much about drought now. The impact of El Niño on country’s monsoon has so far been relatively limited, particularly in the hills. While rainfall has been lower in the Tarai, the hills have continued to receive enough rain,” he said.

He said this is consistent with his observations from previous El Niño years, when its impact was generally weaker in Nepal’s mountain regions. Although the current El Niño is considered stronger, its expected effects on Nepal’s monsoon have not been as severe as feared.

Dahal said the monsoon arrived late this year and rainfall could decline further after mid-August, based on current wind patterns. However, he said it is too early to draw conclusions about the entire monsoon season, which lasts four months.

Madhukar Adhikari said the rainfall has varied significantly by region. While some areas have received plenty of rain, parts of western Nepal, including around Nepalgunj and Surkhet, have received much less, with reports of farmers struggling to plant rice. He stressed that below-average rainfall does not necessarily mean every area will receive less rain, as the distribution of rainfall is also important for livelihoods.

He said that although people were worried that El Niño could cause a severe drought this year, the overall situation has so far been better than feared. Good pre-monsoon rainfall helped reduce the impact of the late monsoon, although localised dry conditions are still visible in some areas. “Whatever has happened so far has generally been in our favour,” Adhikari said, adding that the situation should still be monitored as the season progresses.

Barun Paudel, a senior meteorologist at DHM said El Niño is one of the major global factors affecting the monsoon and can weaken monsoon winds and reduce the regular, widespread rainfall expected during the season. Data from previous El Niño years also show that Nepal generally receives less rainfall during such years.

Paudel said the final assessment of El Niño’s impact will only be possible after the monsoon ends.

मधेश प्रदेशमे देश भरिमे सबसँ कम सापेक्षिक वर्षा भेल अछि, जाहिमे एहि अवधिमे सामान्य वर्षाक मात्र ८१.९ प्रतिशत वर्षा भेल अछि । तहिना कोशी प्रांत के तराई पट्टी मे काफी घाटा देखल गेल, जे मानक मौसमी वर्षा के मात्र 76 प्रतिशत पर संचालित भेल।

देशव्यापी कमी के बावजूद स्थानीयकृत झमाझम बरखा के कारण चुनिंदा पहाड़ी आ पहाड़ी जेब में भारी बरखा भेल अछि. कोशी प्रांत के नुम सन स्टेशन पर 1,567 मिमी बरखा भेल, जखन कि पोखरा के मालेपाटन मे 1,379.2 मिमी बरखा भेल अछि।

कुल मिला कए देश भरि मे वर्षा काफी लगातार रहल अछि, हालांकि इ सामान्य स किछु कम अछि। डीएचएम के अनुसार किछु इलाका मे भारी बरखा दर्ज कायल गेल अछि।

जलवायु विश्लेषक न्गमिन्द्र दाहाल कहलनि जे एल नीनो तापमान सं जुड़ल किछु चीज अछि. तापमान बदलला पर नमी, जलवाष्प आ हवा के पैटर्न पर असर पड़ैत अछि । अस्तु, प्राथमिक कारक तापमान थिक, जे ऐतिहासिक रूप सं एखन अत्यंत उच्च स्तर पर अछि. वायुमंडलीय प्रणाली आरू नमी केरऽ बढ़ोत्तरी प॑ एकरऽ प्रभाव भी होय रहलऽ छै, लेकिन वू गौण प्रभाव छै । तृतीयक प्रभाव एकरऽ प्रभाव छै जे हमरऽ मौजूदा मानसून चक्र प॑ पड़ै छै । जे प्रभाव के तेसर स्तर अछि, ओ जानकारी देलनि।

डीएचएम कहैत रहल अछि जे बरखा औसत स काफी कम होएत। ओ कहलनि जे, आब सूखा के बारे मे ओतेक नहि सुनबा मे आबि रहल अछि, देश के मानसून पर एल नीनो के प्रभाव एखन धरि अपेक्षाकृत सीमित रहल अछि, खास क पहाड़ी पर, तराई मे बरखा कम रहल अछि, पहाड़ी पर पर्याप्त बरखा होइत रहल अछि।

हुनी कहलकै कि ई बात हुनकऽ पिछला एल नीनो सालऽ के अवलोकन के अनुरूप छै, जब॑ एकरऽ प्रभाव आम तौर प॑ नेपाल केरऽ पहाड़ी क्षेत्रऽ म॑ कमजोर छेलै । हालांकि वर्तमान एल नीनो क॑ मजबूत मानलऽ जाय छै, लेकिन नेपाल केरऽ मानसून प॑ एकरऽ अपेक्षित प्रभाव ओतना गंभीर नै रहलऽ छै जेतना कि आशंका छेलै ।

दाहाल कहलनि जे, एहि सालक अंत मे मानसून आयल अछि आ अगस्त के मध्य के बाद बरखा मे आओर कमी आबि सकैत अछि, जे वर्तमान हवा के पैटर्न के आधार पर अछि। हालांकि ओ कहला जे चारि मास तक चलय वाला पूरा मानसून क मौसम क बारे मे निष्कर्ष निकालब एखन जल्दबाजी अछि।

मधुकर अधिकारी कहलनि जे, क्षेत्रक हिसाब सं वर्षा मे काफी अंतर रहल अछि। किछु इलाका मे जतय खूब बरखा भेल अछि ओतहि नेपालगंज आ सुर्खेतक आसपास सहित पश्चिमी नेपालक किछु भाग मे बहुत कम वर्षा भेल अछि, जाहि मे किसान धान रोपबा मे संघर्ष करबाक खबरि अछि। ओ एहि बात पर जोर देलनि जे औसत सं कम बरखा के मतलब ई जरूरी नहि जे हर इलाका मे कम बरखा होएत, किएक त बरखा के वितरण सेहो रोजी-रोटी के लेल महत्वपूर्ण अछि.

हुनी कहलकै कि हालांकि लोगौ क चिंता छै कि एल नीनो स॑ ई साल भयंकर सूखा आबी सकै छै, लेकिन समग्र स्थिति अभी तलक आशंका स॑ बेहतर रहलऽ छै । मानसून सं पहिने नीक वर्षा के कारण देर सं मानसून के प्रभाव के कम करय में मदद भेटल, हालांकि किछु इलाका में स्थानीय शुष्क स्थिति एखनो देखबा में अबैत अछि. अधिकारी कहलनि जे, एखन धरि जे किछु भेल अछि ओ सामान्य तौर पर हमरा सबहक पक्ष मे रहल अछि, मौसम बढ़ैत-बढ़ैत स्थिति पर एखनो नजरि राखल जेबाक चाही।

डीएचएम केरऽ वरिष्ठ मौसम वैज्ञानिक बरुण पौडेल न॑ कहलकै कि एल नीनो मानसून क॑ प्रभावित करै वाला प्रमुख वैश्विक कारकऽ म॑ स॑ एक छै आरू ई मानसून केरऽ हवा क॑ कमजोर करी सकै छै आरू मौसम के दौरान नियमित, व्यापक बारिश के उम्मीद क॑ कम करी सकै छै । पिछला एल नीनो वर्षक आंकड़ा सेहो बताबैत अछि जे नेपाल मे सामान्यतः एहन वर्ष मे कम वर्षा होइत अछि ।

पौडेल न॑ कहलकै कि एल नीनो केरऽ प्रभाव के अंतिम आकलन मानसून खतम होय के बाद ही संभव होतै ।

title: Nepal Police to launch Anti-Cyber Scam Centre amid crime surge - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal Police to launch Anti-Cyber Scam Centre amid crime surge  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug. 12: Nepal Police Headquarters (NPHQ) is preparing to establish an Anti-Cyber Scam Centre (ACSC) and integrated command centres at federal, provincial and district levels as cybercrime continues to rise alongside rapid digitalisation.

Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Abi Narayan Kafle, spokesperson for NPHQ, said the police were prioritising technological capability, human resources and infrastructure to strengthen the response to digital crimes.

The proposed Anti-Cyber Scam Centre, to be established under the Cyber Bureau, will bring together focal representatives from Nepal Police, Nepal Rastra Bank, the Nepal Bankers’ Association, Nepal Telecommunications Authority and internet service providers. The centre is expected to improve information-sharing and coordination

in tackling online scams and financial fraud.

DIG Kafle said the police leadership had given high priority to the initiative in view of the rapid growth and changing nature of cybercrime.

Cybercrime complaints rise

According to the Nepal Police Cyber Bureau, 20,526 cybercrime complaints were registered in the fiscal year 2025/26, an increase of around 1,600 from the previous fiscal year. This means an average of about 56 complaints were received every day. The bureau had recorded 19,730 complaints in FY 2023/24.

Of the complaints registered in FY 2025/26, police filed 409 cases in court for further legal action. The figure was 291 in FY 2024/25 and 255 in FY 2023/24.

“The increase reflects how rapidly criminal activity has shifted towards social media, digital payments, online platforms and other technology-enabled services,” Kafle said.

Inspector General of PoliceDan Bahadur Karki had also said in April that police were receiving around 80 to 90 cybercrime complaints daily, including a significant number related to cyberbullying and online violence.

Cybercrime has become increasingly diverse, with cases involving fake social-media accounts, online blackmail, identity theft, phishing, investment scams, fraudulent online shopping, work-from-home schemes and theft from bank accounts and digital wallets.

Nepal Police plans to establish a cyber-desk at every district police office, recognising that cybercrime can no longer be addressed solely from Kathmandu.

According to Kafle, the move will make the initial handling of cybercrime complaints and digital evidence more accessible while improving the investigative capacity of district police offices.

The police also plan to expand forensic science and digital forensic laboratories to the provincial level and deploy specialised personnel to deal with increasingly complex cyber investigations.

The need for stronger capacity has become more urgent as criminals increasingly exploit digital financial systems. In May, the Cyber Bureau warned the public about fraudulent messages impersonating services such as ConnectIPS and falsely claiming that bank accounts had been locked.

Victims were directed to suspicious links designed to steal personal information and gain unauthorised access to their accounts.

Integrated command centres planned

Beyond cybercrime, Nepal Police is preparing to establish Integrated Command Centres at central, provincial and district levels.

The centres are intended to bring relevant agencies together during emergencies, enabling faster communication, information-sharing and coordinated decision-making.

The initiative forms part of a broader effort to shift Nepal Police from conventional, reactive policing towards a more technology-driven model. For traffic management, the police plan to install GPS systems in patrol teams and vehicles to improve monitoring, deployment and service delivery.

The police also intend to expand the Social Media Coordination Desk to provincial levels to monitor misinformation, disinformation and deepfakes that could trigger communal tensions or create security risks.

Nepal Police is preparing to acquire advanced technologies, including facial-recognition systems, call-interception technology, blockchain-analysis tools and crime-scene scanners.

These technologies are expected to strengthen evidence-based investigations, particularly in cases involving encrypted communications, anonymous accounts, cryptocurrency transactions and multiple digital identities.

According to Kafle, policies are also being prepared for online training, leadership development and performance-based evaluation of police personnel.

The police plan to upgrade their radio communication system and expand an integrated smart CCTV network at urban entry points to improve surveillance and responses to security incidents.

Police Academy nearing completion

The modernisation programme also includes upgrading police training infrastructure.

Construction of the National Police Academy in Panauti, Kavre, being built with a grant from the Government of India, has reached 91 per cent completion, according to Nepal Police.

The project covers 646 ropanis of land out of a total 822 ropanis and includes 67 structures, including 48 buildings.

The academy is expected to provide modern facilities for police training and professional development as Nepal Police prepares its personnel to deal with increasingly sophisticated, technology-driven crime.

title: Nepal Police seeks call interception powers, reviving privacy and civil liberties concerns - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal Police seeks call interception powers, reviving privacy and civil liberties concerns  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal Police has asked the government to give it legal authority to intercept telephone calls and digital communications in real time during criminal investigations, reopening a long-running debate over how far the state should be allowed to ‘intrude’ into citizens’ private communication.

The Police Headquarters in Naxal has incorporated the proposal into its strategic planning framework, arguing that investigators need modern digital tools to pursue criminals who increasingly use encrypted and other sophisticated communication technologies.

The proposal would allow designated police officers to listen to telephone conversations and monitor digital communications in real time if the necessary legal framework and approvals were put in place.

“Individuals involved in heinous crimes or those evading justice often employ advanced technologies, making it necessary for us to listen in on communications when probing serious offences,” Deputy Inspector General Abi Narayan Kafle, central spokesperson for Nepal Police, told Kantipur. “We have prepared a comprehensive plan to make police investigations technology-friendly and have already briefed the Ministry of Home Affairs on this operational strategy.”

Police officials say the proposed power would be aimed at serious criminal investigations rather than broad surveillance. But the request has revived concerns among lawyers and civil rights activists over the possibility of political or institutional abuse, particularly given Nepal’s history of political interference in security and law enforcement agencies.

The proposal also echoes previous attempts by state agencies to obtain wider surveillance powers, which were abandoned after strong opposition from lawmakers, rights activists and civil society groups.

The National Investigation Department, the country’s principal civilian intelligence agency, had previously sought similar authority through proposed legislation. Draft legislation concerning the department had included provisions allowing authorities to monitor, track and intercept phone calls, text messages and video communications.

Section 15 of the proposed intelligence bill would have allowed the chief research officer to order the interception of electronic communications when other intelligence-gathering methods were considered impractical and when failure to intercept the communications was deemed to pose an immediate threat to national security.

The proposal drew widespread criticism over the potential for abuse. Political opposition and public concern eventually forced the government to abandon the bill.

The latest push by the police comes against a different backdrop. Law enforcement officials argue that criminals have become increasingly adept at using technology to conceal their activities, making access to communications an important investigative tool.

But legal experts say any such authority would have to be tightly circumscribed by law and subjected to independent judicial oversight.

Senior Advocate Satish Krishna Kharel, an expert in criminal law, said the potential risks of live interception are considerably greater than those associated with obtaining call detail records or SMS logs.

Police already need judicial authorisation to obtain such records, he said. Allowing investigators to listen to conversations as they happen would create a much greater intrusion into an individual’s privacy.

“Without stringent statutory criteria and robust judicial oversight, this kind of power is exceptionally susceptible to abuse,” Kharel told Kantipur. “Given that agencies like Nepal Police and the NID have historically faced intense political pressure, granting the power to live-tap any citizen’s phone directly compromises the right to privacy guaranteed under Article 28 of the constitution.”

Article 28 of the constitution guarantees the privacy of an individual’s body, residence, property, documents, data, correspondence and personal character. Any law allowing the state to intercept communications would therefore have to operate within those constitutional protections.

The question of how police obtain telecommunications data has already been tested by the Supreme Court.

Before the court intervened, police had obtained call detail records and SMS data through informal arrangements with telecommunications companies, both private and state-owned. That practice came under intense scrutiny after the assassination of Supreme Court Justice Rana Bahadur Bam on May 31, 2012.

During the investigation into the killing, police collected more than 500,000 call records and over 30,000 text messages in an effort to identify the perpetrators.

The broad collection of communications data failed to identify the actual killer while exposing the personal information of thousands of people who had no connection to the crime.

In a landmark ruling, a joint bench of then-Chief Justice Kalyan Shrestha and Justice Devendra Gopal Shrestha held that the need to investigate a crime did not give the state unrestricted authority to access citizens’ communications data.

The ruling established judicial authorisation as a necessary safeguard for obtaining such information, reinforcing the principle that investigative necessity cannot override the constitutional right to privacy.

The judgment has since become an important reference point in discussions about state access to telecommunications data.

Former Inspector General of Police Dhiraj Pratap Singh acknowledged that police had faced disciplinary scrutiny in the past over the improper use of call detail records. But he said the possibility of abuse should not by itself prevent law enforcement from acquiring modern investigative capabilities.

“There have been instances in the past where police faced strict departmental scrutiny for casually accessing call logs,” Singh said. “However, denying an essential investigative mechanism simply because abuse is theoretically possible is not a balanced approach.”

Singh pointed to India and the United States as examples of countries where law enforcement agencies have interception powers subject to statutory restrictions and oversight mechanisms. He argued that Nepal could develop a similarly controlled system rather than leave investigators without tools needed to tackle sophisticated criminal networks.

The distinction between obtaining historical communications data and intercepting communications as they occur is central to the debate.

Call detail records can show information such as the numbers involved in a call, the time and duration of the communication and, depending on the available records, information about the cell tower used. Live interception, by contrast, would give investigators access to the content of communications as they take place.

That difference makes the proposed authority particularly sensitive from a privacy perspective.

Cyber law expert and advocate Baburam Aryal said any law allowing interception would need to specify precisely when and why it could be used.

“The law must explicitly define the exact conditions under which law enforcement can intercept communications and mandate that the specific criminal purpose be legally recorded,” Aryal said. “Granting such authority without transparent, enforceable parameters significantly increases the risk of institutional abuse.”

Police officials insist that they are not seeking unrestricted powers.

A high-ranking official at Police Headquarters said the proposed authority would be used only in targeted criminal investigations and would require judicial approval and independent oversight.

“We are asking for interception powers strictly for targeted criminal investigations, subject to explicit judicial approval and independent regulatory oversight mechanisms,” the official said.

For legal experts, however, the details of those safeguards will be as important as the power itself.

Kharel has proposed a two-tier system of protection. First, permission to intercept communications should come from an independent judicial authority outside the police, military and intelligence establishments. Second, the system should require public reporting after a specified period so that unlawful or politically motivated surveillance could eventually be exposed.

Such safeguards, he argued, would help prevent interception powers from becoming a tool for monitoring political opponents, journalists, activists or other citizens unrelated to criminal investigations.

The police proposal therefore presents the government with a difficult policy choice.

Law enforcement agencies want greater access to digital communications as crime becomes more technology-dependent.

Meanwhile, Nepal’s constitutional framework and judicial history impose significant limits on the state’s ability to intrude into private communications.

सिंह कहला जे पहिने एहन मामला सामने आयल अछि जखन पुलिस कए कॉल लॉग कए लापरवाही स पहुंचबा लेल विभागीय कड़ा जांच क सामना करय पड़ैत छल। “हालांकि, खाली ई लेली कि दुर्व्यवहार सैद्धांतिक रूप स॑ संभव छै, एक आवश्यक जांच तंत्र स॑ इनकार करना कोनो संतुलित दृष्टिकोण नै छै।”

सिंह न॑ भारत आरू अमेरिका क॑ ऐसनऽ देशऽ के उदाहरण के रूप म॑ इंगित करलकै, जहां कानून प्रवर्तन एजेंसी क॑ वैधानिक प्रतिबंध आरू निगरानी तंत्र के अधीन अवरोधन शक्ति छै । हुनकऽ तर्क छेलै कि नेपाल जांचकर्ता सिनी क॑ परिष्कृत आपराधिक नेटवर्क स॑ निपटै लेली जरूरी औजार के बिना छोड़ी क॑ ऐन्हऽ ही नियंत्रित प्रणाली विकसित करी सकै छै ।

ऐतिहासिक संचार आँकड़ा प्राप्त करनाय आ संचार कें घटित होय कें अनुसार ओकरा रोकय कें बीच कें भेद बहस कें केंद्रीय छै.

कॉल डिटेल रिकॉर्ड कॉल मे शामिल नंबर, संचार कें समय आ अवधि आ उपलब्ध रिकॉर्ड कें आधार पर उपयोग कैल गेल सेल टावर कें बारे मे जानकारी जैना जानकारी देखा सकय छै. एकरऽ विपरीत लाइव इंटरसेप्शन स॑ जांचकर्ता सिनी क॑ संचार केरऽ सामग्री तलक पहुँच मिलतै, कैन्हेंकि ई संचार घटित होय छै ।

ओ अंतर प्रस्तावित प्राधिकारी कें गोपनीयता कें दृष्टिकोण सं विशेष रूप सं संवेदनशील बनायत छै.

साइबर कानून विशेषज्ञ आरू अधिवक्ता बाबुराम अर्यल नँ कहलकै कि इंटरसेप्शन के अनुमति दै वाला कोनो भी कानून क ई ठीक-ठीक बताबै के जरूरत होतै कि एकरौ उपयोग कहिया आरू किया करलौ जाब॑ सकै छै ।

अर्यल नँ कहलकै, “कानून मँ स्पष्ट रूप सँ ई परिभाषित करना चाहिय्यौ कि कानून प्रवर्तन क कोनौ सटीक शर्तौ के तहत संचार क रोकै सकै छै आरू विशिष्ट आपराधिक उद्देश्य क कानूनी तौर प दर्ज करै के आदेश देना चाहिय्यौ । “पारदर्शी, प्रवर्तनीय पैरामीटर के बिना ऐसनऽ अधिकार प्रदान करला स॑ संस्थागत दुरुपयोग के खतरा काफी बढ़ी जाय छै ।”

पुलिस अधिकारी के कहनाय छनि जे ओ अप्रतिबंधित अधिकार के मांग नहि क रहल छथिन्ह.

पुलिस मुख्यालय केरऽ एगो उच्च पदस्थ अधिकारी न॑ कहलकै कि प्रस्तावित प्राधिकरण केरऽ इस्तेमाल केवल लक्षित आपराधिक जांच म॑ ही करलऽ जैतै आरू एकरा लेली न्यायिक मंजूरी आरू स्वतंत्र निगरानी के जरूरत होतै ।

अधिकारी नँ कहलकै, “हम लक्षित आपराधिक जांच लेली सख्ती स॑ इंटरसेप्शन पावर मँगै छियै, जे स्पष्ट न्यायिक मंजूरी आरू स्वतंत्र नियामक निगरानी तंत्र के अधीन छै ।

मुदा कानूनी विशेषज्ञक लेल ओहि सुरक्षा उपायक विवरण ओतबे महत्वपूर्ण होयत जतेक कि स्वयं सत्ता।

खरेल सुरक्षा के दू स्तरीय प्रणाली प्रस्तावित केने छथि। पहिल, संचार कें रोकय कें अनुमति पुलिस, सैन्य आ खुफिया प्रतिष्ठानक सं बाहर कोनों स्वतंत्र न्यायिक प्राधिकारी सं भेटबाक चाही. दोसर, प्रणाली कें लेल एकटा निर्धारित अवधि कें बाद सार्वजनिक रिपोर्टिंग कें आवश्यकता होबाक चाही ताकि अंततः गैरकानूनी या राजनीतिक रूप सं प्रेरित निगरानी कें उजागर कैल जा सकय.

हुनकऽ तर्क छेलै कि ऐसनऽ सुरक्षा स॑ इंटरसेप्शन पावर क॑ राजनीतिक विरोधी, पत्रकार, कार्यकर्ता या आपराधिक जांच स॑ असंबंधित अन्य नागरिकऽ प॑ नजर रखै के उपकरण नै बनै स॑ रोकै म॑ मदद मिलतै ।

एहि लेल पुलिस प्रस्ताव सरकार क सामने एकटा कठिन नीतिगत विकल्प पेश करैत अछि।

कानून प्रवर्तन एजेंसी डिजिटल संचार कें बेसि पहुंच चाहय छै, कियाकि अपराध बेसि तकनीक पर निर्भर भ जायत छै.

एम्हर नेपालक संवैधानिक ढाँचा आ न्यायिक इतिहास राज्यक निजी संचार मे घुसपैठ करबाक क्षमता पर महत्वपूर्ण सीमा लगा दैत अछि ।

title: Foreign medical students come to Nepal but twice as many Nepalis pursue medicine abroad - The Kathmandu Post
description: Foreign medical students come to Nepal but twice as many Nepalis pursue medicine abroad  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal is attracting a growing number of foreign students to its medical colleges, particularly for MBBS and postgraduate programmes, even as thousands of Nepali students continue to leave the country to study medicine.

Data from the Medical Education Commission show that a total of 1,859 foreign students enrolled in medical education programmes in Nepal between 2024 and 2026. During the same period, as many as 4,741 Nepali students obtained approval from the commission to pursue medical education abroad.

Arjun Dhakal, information officer at the commission, however said that the figure of students approved to go abroad should not be read as the actual number who left Nepal, because not everyone who receives approval necessarily travels abroad for study.

MBBS (bachelor of medicine and bachelor of surgery) accounts for the largest share of movement in both directions. In the three-year period, 1,766 foreign students enrolled in MBBS programmes in Nepal, rising from 572 in 2024 to 770 in 2026. The figures suggest that Nepal’s medical colleges are becoming more attractive to foreign students, but not enough to fill the seats reserved for them.

The contrast is especially clear in other health programmes. Foreign students have been allocated seats in BDS (bachelor of dental surgery), BNS (bachelor of nursing science), BSc Nursing, BAMS (bachelor of Ayurvedic medicine and surgery), BPH (bachelor of public health) and B Pharm, among others, but not a single foreign student enrolled in these programmes in 2026. Even Nepali students did not fully occupy seats in some of these courses.

India is both the largest source of foreign students coming to Nepal for medical education and the leading destination for Nepali students pursuing medical studies abroad, according to data from the commission.

Nearly half of the Nepali students who obtained permission to pursue medical education abroad—from undergraduate and postgraduate programmes to doctoral studies—went to India. Over the three-year period, 1,677 students received approval to study in India, including around 1,350 pursuing MBBS and nursing.

Dhakal attributed the high number partly to Nepal’s recognition of India’s National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), which makes it easier for Nepali students to seek admission to Indian medical institutions. The open border and relatively easy movement between the two countries are other factors, he said.

“India is more accessible because of the open border and the ease of travel between the two countries,” said Dhakal.

Bangladesh was the second-most popular destination. More than 450 Nepali students went there to study medical education during the three-year period. Australia, China, the Philippines, the United States and the United Kingdom followed, with more than 100 students going to each of these countries for medical studies.

Most of those going abroad enrolled in undergraduate programmes, although some received scholarships, Dhakal said. The number of Nepali students receiving approval to study abroad fluctuated over the three years. In 2024, 1,515 students obtained permission, compared with 1,815 in 2025 and 1,411 in 2026.

Overall, only 26.59 percent of the seats set aside for foreign students were filled, according to commission data. The Medical Education Act 2019 allows up to one-third of total seats in undergraduate and postgraduate medical education to be allocated to foreign students.

According to undergraduate enrolment data, enrolment increased by 34 percent between 2024 and 2026. In 2024, medical colleges had 7,606 seats, of which 6,343 were filled. The number of seats rose to 8,070 in 2025, with 7,196 students admitted. In 2026, a total of 8,550 students enrolled against 9,273 available seats.

Shreekrishna Giri, a former vice-chairperson and current member of the Medical Education Commission, said Nepal had considerable potential to attract foreign medical students and that their numbers were gradually increasing. However, he cautioned against compromising academic standards in the drive to expand enrolment.

At postgraduate level, enrolment rose by around 22 percent over the three-year period. In 2024, 1,467 students enrolled out of 1,724 available seats. The number of seats increased to 2,086 in 2025, when 1,750 students enrolled. In 2026, 1,789 students enrolled out of 2,056 seats.

Although both the number of seats and total enrolment have increased, medical colleges have continued to struggle to fill all the seats approved by the commission. According to the commission, between 700 and 1,200 undergraduate seats and roughly 250 to 325 postgraduate seats remained vacant in the three years.

A particularly large number of seats reserved for foreign students remain unfilled. In 2026, 2,428 undergraduate seats were allocated to foreign students, but only 476 were filled, leaving 1,952 vacant. Under the existing provision, seats left vacant by foreign students can be offered to Nepali students.

The Private Medical and Dental College Association has called for an increase in the quota for foreign students. The association submitted a memorandum to Health and Food Safety Minister Nisha Mehta on July 30, seeking an expansion of the seats allocated to foreign students.

Association president Dr Gyanendra Man Singh Karki said the government should increase the quota if it wants to attract more foreign students. He said Nepal could enrol large numbers of foreign students in MBBS programmes if the government introduced clear policies and programmes.

Karki said Nepal could attract a significant number of Indian students if the government took the initiative to reach an agreement with India. Sri Lanka and the Maldives could also be potential sources of students for MBBS and MD programmes, he said.

“The Nepal government has made no real effort to attract foreign students. The entrance examination and admission process here have also become cumbersome. If the process is made easier, we can bring in as many foreign students as we want,” said Karki. “Foreign students also bring foreign currency which contributes to the country’s economy.”

Stakeholders and medical education experts, however, say increasing the number of seats alone should not be the priority. They argue that Nepal must first ensure the quality of medical education and the adequacy of infrastructure.

Giri said the number of foreign students could increase significantly if Nepal secures recognition from the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME), which would strengthen the international credibility of its medical education.

“Nepal has already moved ahead with the process of obtaining recognition. A team from the federation has also visited Nepal and made suggestions for some improvements. If those recommendations are addressed, Nepal can obtain recognition,” said Giri. “Once that happens, the credibility of Nepal’s medical education will increase internationally, and foreign students will be more interested in coming here.”

Giri warned that increasing seats beyond established standards simply to attract foreign students could undermine quality. “Medical education directly affects the health of every citizen. We must ensure minimum standards. Medical education is different from other disciplines. We cannot run medical education merely to produce people who obtain a licence,” he said. “Quality cannot be compromised. Medical education should not be viewed only in terms of money.”

Medical college operators, meanwhile, argue that seat numbers should be increased gradually in line with the availability of infrastructure and compliance with prescribed standards.

Karki said the state should adopt a clear policy to attract foreign students while ensuring that the necessary legal and administrative procedures are in place. “By educating foreign students, Nepali students also receive scholarships equivalent to 10 percent of the seats,” said Karki.

Dr Rajendra Koju, a professor at Kathmandu University School of Medical Sciences, said any increase in seats should be based on demonstrable improvements in quality. “If quality is improved continuously, the number of students will increase on its own. If we focus only on increasing numbers without paying attention to quality, our credibility will decline,” said Koju.

He said seat numbers could be adjusted after assessing the number of patients available for clinical training and the physical and academic infrastructure of medical colleges. “Whether seats should be increased or reduced is directly linked to quality. That must always be considered when making such decisions,” he said.

Dr Manoj Humagain, dean of the Kathmandu University School of Medical Sciences, also said seat expansion should follow the fulfilment of infrastructure and other regulatory requirements. He said the relatively lower cost of MBBS education in Nepal compared with neighbouring countries had helped increase foreign students’ interest in Nepali medical colleges.

“Seats can be increased once the required infrastructure and standards are met. There is interest among foreign students. If their quota is increased, the scholarship quota for Nepali students can also be expanded,” said Humagain.

नेपाल अपन मेडिकल कॉलेज मे बढ़ैत संख्या मे विदेशी छात्र कए आकर्षित क रहल अछि, खास कए एमबीबीएस आ स्नातकोत्तर कार्यक्रम लेल, एतय तक कि हजारों नेपाली छात्र मेडिसिन क पढ़ाई लेल देश छोड़ि कए जारी अछि।

चिकित्सा शिक्षा आयोग केरऽ आंकड़ा बताबै छै कि २०२४ स॑ २०२६ के बीच नेपाल म॑ कुल १,८५९ विदेशी छात्र न॑ चिकित्सा शिक्षा कार्यक्रम म॑ नामांकन करलकै ।एही दौरान ४,७४१ नेपाली छात्रऽ न॑ विदेशऽ म॑ चिकित्सा शिक्षा लेली आयोग स॑ मंजूरी प्राप्त करलकै ।

आयोगके सूचना अधिकारी अर्जुन ढकाल ओना कहलनि जे विदेश जेबाक लेल स्वीकृत छात्रक आंकड़ा के नेपाल छोड़निहार वास्तविक संख्या नहि पढ़बाक चाही, कारण स्वीकृति भेटनिहार सब गोटे पढ़ाई लेल विदेश यात्रा करब जरूरी नहि अछि।

एमबीबीएस (बैचलर ऑफ मेडिसिन आ बैचलर ऑफ सर्जरी) के हिस्सा दुनू दिशा में सब सं बेसी अछि. तीन वर्षक अवधि मे नेपाल मे एमबीबीएस कार्यक्रम मे 1766 विदेशी छात्रक नामांकन भेल, जे 2024 मे 572 छल आ 2026 मे 770 भ गेल।आँकड़ा स इ बुझना जाइत अछि जे नेपाल क मेडिकल कॉलेज विदेशी छात्र क लेल बेसी आकर्षक भ रहल अछि, मुदा हुनका लेल आरक्षित सीट कए भरबा लेल पर्याप्त नहि अछि।

एकर विपरीत विशेष रूप सं अन्य स्वास्थ्य कार्यक्रम मे स्पष्ट छै. विदेशी छात्रक कें बीडीएस (दंत सर्जरी कें स्नातक), बीएनएस (नर्सिंग विज्ञान कें स्नातक), बीएससी नर्सिंग, बीएएमएस (आयुर्वेदिक चिकित्सा आ सर्जरी कें स्नातक), बीपीएच (जनस्वास्थ्य कें स्नातक) आ बी फार्म, आ अन्य मे सीट आवंटित कैल गेल छै, मुदा 2026 मे एकटा विदेशी छात्र कें एहि कार्यक्रम मे नामांकन नहि भेल छै.एतय तक कि नेपाली एहि मे स किछु कोर्स मे छात्र पूरा तरह स सीट नहि लेने छलाह।

आयोग केरऽ आंकड़ऽ के अनुसार भारत चिकित्सा शिक्षा लेली नेपाल आबै वाला विदेशी छात्रऽ के सबसें बड़ऽ स्रोत आरू विदेशऽ म॑ चिकित्सा के पढ़ाई करै वाला नेपाली छात्रऽ लेली अग्रणी गंतव्य दूनू छै ।

विदेश मे चिकित्सा शिक्षा के अनुमति प्राप्त करय वाला नेपाली छात्र मे सं लगभग आधा-स्नातक आ स्नातकोत्तर कार्यक्रम सं लsक डॉक्टरेट के पढ़ाई तक-भारत गेलाह. तीन साल क अवधि मे भारत मे पढ़ाई क लेल 1677 छात्र कए मंजूरी भेटल, जाहि मे करीब 1350 छात्र एमबीबीएस आ नर्सिंग करैत छथि।

ढकल न॑ ई अधिक संख्या के कुछ हद तलक भारत केरऽ राष्ट्रीय पात्रता सह प्रवेश परीक्षा (नीट) क॑ नेपाल केरऽ मान्यता के कारण बतैलकै, जेकरा स॑ नेपाली छात्रऽ क॑ भारतीय चिकित्सा संस्थान म॑ प्रवेश लेली आसान होय ​​जाय छै । ओ कहलनि जे, दुनू देशक बीच खुला सीमा आ अपेक्षाकृत सहज आवागमन अन्य कारक अछि।

ढकल कहलनि जे, खुला सीमा आ दुनू देशक बीच यात्रा मे सहजताक कारण भारत बेसी सुलभ अछि।

बांग्लादेश दोसर सबसँ लोकप्रिय गंतव्य छल । तीन वर्षक अवधि मे ४५० सँ बेसी नेपाली छात्र चिकित्सा शिक्षाक अध्ययन लेल ओतय गेल छल । एकरऽ बाद ऑस्ट्रेलिया, चीन, फिलीपींस, अमेरिका आरू यूनाइटेड किंगडम भी ऐलै, जेकरा म॑ १०० स॑ भी अधिक छात्र चिकित्सा केरऽ पढ़ाई लेली ई हर देश म॑ गेलऽ छेलै ।

विदेश जेबाक अधिकांश लोक स्नातक कार्यक्रम मे नामांकन केलथि, हालांकि किछु गोटे कए छात्रवृत्ति भेटल छल, धकाल कहला। तीन वर्ष मे विदेश मे पढ़ाई लेल स्वीकृति प्राप्त करय वाला नेपाली छात्रक संख्या मे उतार-चढ़ाव भेल। 2024 मे 1515 छात्र अनुमति प्राप्त केलथि, जखन कि 2025 मे 1815 आ 2026 मे 1411 छात्र अनुमति प्राप्त केलथि।

आयोग क आंकड़ा क अनुसार कुल मिला कए विदेशी छात्र क लेल राखल गेल सीट मे स मात्र 26.59 प्रतिशत सीट भरल गेल। मेडिकल एजुकेशन एक्ट 2019 मे स्नातक आ स्नातकोत्तर मेडिकल शिक्षा मे कुल सीट क एक तिहाई तक विदेशी छात्र कए आवंटित करबाक अनुमति अछि।

स्नातक नामांकन के आंकड़ा के अनुसार 2024 सं 2026 के बीच नामांकन मे 34 प्रतिशत के बढ़ोतरी भेल अछि.2024 मे मेडिकल कॉलेज मे 7606 सीट छल, जाहि मे सं 6343 सीट भरल छल. 2025 मे सीट क संख्या बढ़ि कए 8070 भ गेल, जाहि मे 7196 छात्र कए प्रवेश लेल गेल। 2026 मे कुल 8,550 छात्र क नामांकन भेल छल, जखन कि 9,273 सीट उपलब्ध छल।

चिकित्सा शिक्षा आयोगके पूर्व उपाध्यक्ष आ वर्तमान सदस्य श्रीकृष्ण गिरी नेपालमे विदेशी मेडिकल छात्रके आकर्षित करबाक काफी सम्भावना रहल आ ओकर संख्या धीरे-धीरे बढि रहल बतौलनि । हालांकि ओ नामांकन विस्तार क अभियान मे शैक्षणिक मानक स समझौता करबा स चेतावनी देलथि।

स्नातकोत्तर स्तर पर तीन साल क अवधि मे नामांकन मे करीब 22 प्रतिशत क बढ़ोतरी भेल। 2024 मे उपलब्ध 1724 सीट मे स 1467 छात्र क नामांकन भेल। 2025 मे सीट क संख्या बढ़ि कए 2086 भ गेल, जखन 1750 छात्र क नामांकन भेल। 2026 मे 2056 सीट मे स 1789 छात्र क नामांकन भेल।

हालांकि सीट के संख्या आओर कुल नामांकन दुनू बढ़ि गेल अछि मुदा आयोग के मंजूर सभ सीट के भरय लेल मेडिकल कॉलेज के संघर्ष जारी अछि. आयोग के अनुसार तीन साल मे 700 सं 1200 स्नातक सीट आओर मोटा-मोटी 250 सं 325 स्नातकोत्तर सीट खाली रहल.

विदेशी छात्र क लेल आरक्षित विशेष रूप स पैघ संख्या मे सीट अभरल अछि। 2026 मे 2,428 स्नातक सीट विदेशी छात्र कए आवंटित कैल गेल छल, मुदा मात्र 476 सीट भरल गेल, जाहि स 1,952 सीट खाली रहि गेल। मौजूदा प्रावधान के तहत विदेशी छात्र द्वारा खाली छोड़ल गेल सीट नेपाली छात्र के देल जा सकैत अछि।

प्राइवेट मेडिकल एंड डेंटल कॉलेज एसोसिएशन विदेशी छात्र क कोटा बढ़ेबाक आह्वान केलक अछि। एसोसिएशन 30 जुलाई कए स्वास्थ्य आ खाद्य सुरक्षा मंत्री निशा मेहता कए ज्ञापन देलक, जाहि मे विदेशी छात्र कए आवंटित सीट क विस्तार करबाक मांग कैल गेल छल।

एसोसिएशन के अध्यक्ष डॉ. ज्ञानेन्द्र मान सिंह कार्की कहलनि जे, सरकार बेसी विदेशी छात्र के आकर्षित करय चाहैत अछि त कोटा बढ़ाबय के चाही। ओ कहलनि जे, सरकार यदि स्पष्ट नीति आ कार्यक्रम लागू करत त नेपाल एमबीबीएस कार्यक्रम मे पैघ संख्या मे विदेशी छात्र के नामांकन क सकैत अछि।

कार्की कहलनि जे, यदि सरकार भारत सं समझौता करबाक पहल करत त नेपाल उल्लेखनीय संख्या मे भारतीय छात्र के आकर्षित क सकैत अछि। हुनी कहलकै कि श्रीलंका आरू मालदीव भी एमबीबीएस आरू एमडी कार्यक्रम लेली छात्रऽ के संभावित स्रोत बनी सकै छै ।

कार्की कहलनि जे, नेपाल सरकार विदेशी छात्र के आकर्षित करय लेल कोनो वास्तविक प्रयास नहि केलक अछि, एहि ठामक प्रवेश परीक्षा आ प्रवेश प्रक्रिया सेहो बोझिल भ गेल अछि, यदि प्रक्रिया आसान भ गेल त हम सब जतेक विदेशी छात्र चाहैत छी ओतेक आनि सकैत छी। “विदेशी छात्र विदेशी मुद्रा सेहो अनैत छथि जे देशक अर्थव्यवस्था मे योगदान दैत अछि।”

हालांकि हितधारक आ चिकित्सा शिक्षा विशेषज्ञ क कहब अछि जे केवल सीट क संख्या बढ़ाबय कए प्राथमिकता नहि हेबाक चाही। हुनकऽ तर्क छै कि नेपाल क॑ सबसें पहल॑ चिकित्सा शिक्षा के गुणवत्ता आरू बुनियादी ढांचा के पर्याप्तता सुनिश्चित करना चाहियऽ ।

गिरी कहलनि जे, नेपाल विश्व चिकित्सा शिक्षा महासंघ (डब्ल्यूएफएमई) सं मान्यता प्राप्त करत त विदेशी छात्रक संख्या काफी बढ़ि सकैत अछि, जाहि सं ओकर चिकित्सा शिक्षा के अंतर्राष्ट्रीय विश्वसनीयता मजबूत होयत।

गिरि कहलनि जे, नेपाल मान्यता प्राप्त करबाक प्रक्रिया मे आगू बढ़ि चुकल अछि, महासंघक एकटा टीम सेहो नेपाल भ्रमण कए किछु सुधारक सुझाव देलक अछि, जँ ओहि सिफारिश सभ केँ संबोधित कयल जाय तऽ नेपाल मान्यता प्राप्त क’ सकैत अछि। “एक बेर एहन भेला पर नेपालक मेडिकल शिक्षाक विश्वसनीयता अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर बढ़त, आ विदेशी छात्र एहि ठाम एबा मे बेसी रुचि लेताह।”

गिरी न॑ चेतावनी देलकै कि खाली विदेशी छात्रऽ क॑ आकर्षित करै लेली स्थापित मानक स॑ आगू के सीट बढ़ाबै स॑ गुणवत्ता प॑ असर पड़॑ सकै छै । ओ कहलनि जे, चिकित्सा शिक्षा के सीधा असर हर नागरिक के स्वास्थ्य पर पड़ैत अछि, हमरा सब के न्यूनतम मानक सुनिश्चित करय पड़त, चिकित्सा शिक्षा अन्य विषय स अलग अछि, हम सब सिर्फ लाइसेंस प्राप्त करय वाला लोक के पैदा करय लेल मेडिकल शिक्षा नहि चला सकैत छी। “गुणवत्ता के साथ समझौता नै करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै, मेडिकल शिक्षा क॑ खाली पैसा के हिसाब स॑ नै देखलऽ जाय।”

ओतहि मेडिकल कॉलेज संचालक क तर्क अछि जे बुनियादी ढांचा क उपलब्धता आ निर्धारित मानक क अनुपालन क अनुरूप सीट क संख्या धीरे-धीरे बढ़ाउल जाए।

कार्की कहलनि जे, राज्य के विदेशी छात्र के आकर्षित करय लेल स्पष्ट नीति अपनाबय के चाही, संगहि ई सुनिश्चित करबाक चाही जे आवश्यक कानूनी आ प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया कायम अछि। कार्की कहलनि जे, विदेशी छात्र के शिक्षित क नेपाली छात्र के सेहो 10 प्रतिशत सीट के बराबर छात्रवृत्ति भेटैत अछि।

काठमांडू विश्वविद्यालय मेडिकल साइंसेज स्कूल के प्राध्यापक डॉ. राजेन्द्र कोजू सीट मे कोनो तरहक वृद्धि गुणवत्ता मे प्रदर्शन योग्य सुधार के आधार पर हेबाक चाही बतौलनि । कोजू कहला जे अगर गुणवत्ता मे लगातार सुधार होएत त छात्र क संख्या अपने आप बढ़ि जाएत, गुणवत्ता पर ध्यान नहि देने अगर हम केवल संख्या बढ़ेबा पर ध्यान देब त हमर विश्वसनीयता मे गिरावट आओत।

ओ कहला जे क्लिनिकल ट्रेनिंग लेल उपलब्ध मरीज क संख्या आ मेडिकल कॉलेज क शारीरिक आ शैक्षणिक बुनियादी ढांचा क आकलन क बाद सीट नंबर मे समायोजन कैल जा सकैत अछि। ओ कहला जे सीट बढ़ेबाक चाही या कम करबाक सीधा संबंध गुणवत्ता स अछि, एहि तरहक फैसला लैत काल सदिखन ओहि पर विचार करबाक चाही।

काठमांडू विश्वविद्यालय मेडिकल साइंसेज स्कूल के डीन डॉ. मनोज हुमागैन सेहो कहलनि जे, सीट विस्तार मे बुनियादी ढांचा आ अन्य नियामक आवश्यकता पूरा भेला पर हेबाक चाही। ओ कहलनि जे, पड़ोसी देशक तुलना मे नेपाल मे एमबीबीएस शिक्षाक अपेक्षाकृत कम लागत सँ विदेशी छात्रक नेपाली मेडिकल कॉलेज मे रुचि बढ़ेबा मे मदद भेटल अछि।

हुमागैन कहलनि जे, आवश्यक बुनियादी ढांचा आ मानक पूरा भेला पर सीट बढ़ाओल जा सकैत अछि, विदेशी छात्र मे रुचि अछि, हुनकर कोटा बढल गेल त नेपाली छात्रक छात्रवृत्ति कोटा सेहो विस्तारित कएल जा सकैत अछि।

full_article:
Kathmandu. There is currently an extreme shortage of LP gas for cooking across the country, including the Kathmandu Valley. Long queues of consumers have been seen at gas depots since early morning. The issue of gas is being discussed everywhere, from the streets to the parliament.

Everyone is interested in when gas will be available easily. According to the government and gas industrialists, the supply of gas in the market is gradually becoming easier, but it is expected to take about a month for the situation to return to normal, with no need for consumers to queue.

The main reasons for the current gas shortage in the market are the sudden pressure on the supply chain and consumer psychology. Due to the escalating conflict in West Asia (Middle East), the supply of gas was affected, leading the Nepal Oil Corporation's board of directors to decide on February 29 to sell and distribute only half cylinders (7.1 kg) of gas.

Distributing half cylinders of gas allowed more consumers' kitchens to be lit with a smaller amount of gas. A kind of balance was maintained in the market.

However, as the import of gas became somewhat easier, the corporation resumed the distribution of the usual 14.2 kg full cylinder gas from July 31. Consumers who had previously faced shortages started buying gas in large numbers as soon as they could get full cylinders. Consumers brought all their empty cylinders to the market. Stakeholders say that the balance created when half cylinders were sent to the market was disrupted as soon as full cylinder sales began, and suddenly it became difficult to get gas.

According to Dewan Bahadur Chand, Chairman of the Nepal LP Gas Industry Association, consumers will feel some ease in gas supply within the next two to three days, but it will take another month for the market to return to a completely normal state.

According to Chairman Chand, the arrival of gas bullets from India has increased recently. On Monday alone, about 115 to 125 bullets entered Nepal, and on Tuesday, 90 to 95 gas bullets are passing through the Birgunj border.

"Due to maintenance work at India's Barauni Refinery, only 10-15 vehicles were coming daily from there in the past, but on Monday, 48 filled bullets came from there," said Chairman Chand, "Most of them are for the Kathmandu Valley. Gas loaded from Barauni will reach the market within 3 days."

Besides this, gas is also coming from Paradip (Odisha), India. However, since the distance from there to Nepal is about 1250 km, it takes up to 10 days for the loaded gas to reach the consumers. Although gas from Haldia and Durgapur in India has stopped, industrialists say that the supply from Mathura has been slightly increased.

To meet the market demand, Nepal Oil Corporation has also increased the import quota. The quota, which was 50,000 metric tons last month, has been increased to 55,000 metric tons this month. Chand says that even though about 130 to 140 vehicles are being loaded daily, the market will not become 100% normal immediately.

"About 30,000 metric tons of gas were imported less in the last two months, which affected the market. It will take more time to refill all those empty cylinders now," he said.

'Gas quota increased by more than 15 percent'

Currently, to reduce the gas shortage in the market, arrangements have been made to distribute gas to consumers through Nepal Gas, Sugam, Everest, Shriram, Sagar Gas, and Salt Trading Corporation (STC) from the depot in Teku.

According to Manoj Thakur, spokesperson for Nepal Oil Corporation, 800 to 1250 cylinders are being sold daily from Teku. He informed that the corporation has requested more gas than its regular quota, and the Indian side has stated that they can supply up to 55,000 metric tons per month.

In normal times, 48,000 metric tons of gas were consumed. "If we look at our data and the data from the customs department, more gas is being imported than is being consumed, by 10 to 15 percent. More than a hundred bullets are passing daily," said Thakur.

However, there are some practical problems in distribution. Although gas is given at Teku after recording names and numbers, it has been found that some people come to get gas two to three times a day, carrying it on bicycles. Real consumers are facing hardship because many people from the same household queue up and workers carry multiple cylinders of gas.

Those involved in black marketeering will be punished

While efforts are being made for the smooth supply of gas, those involved in black marketing by taking advantage of this shortage are also active. The corporation has received complaints that a gang is active, closing their shop shutters during the day and saying 'no gas', and selling gas at high prices secretly at night.

"We will take the help of the police to control such black marketers," said spokesperson Thakur, "We will deploy police, conduct raids, and take strict action against those who are engaged in the wrong practice of telling consumers there is no gas but sending it secretly."

काठमांडू। एखन काठमांडू घाटी सहित देश भरि मे खाना बनाबय लेल एलपी गैस के अत्यधिक कमी अछि. भोरे स गैस डिपो पर उपभोक्ता क लंबा कतार देखबा मे आबि रहल अछि। गली स ल कए संसद तक सब ठाम गैस क मुद्दा पर चर्चा भ रहल अछि।

सबके रुचि अछि जे गैस कहिया आसानी स उपलब्ध होएत। सरकार आ गैस उद्योगपति क अनुसार बाजार मे गैस क आपूर्ति धीरे-धीरे आसान भ रहल अछि, मुदा स्थिति सामान्य होबय मे करीब एक मास लागबाक उम्मीद अछि, जाहि मे उपभोक्ता कए कतार बनेबाक जरूरत नहि अछि।

बाजार मे वर्तमान गैस क कमी क मुख्य कारण आपूर्ति श्रृंखला आ उपभोक्ता मनोविज्ञान पर अचानक दबाव अछि। पश्चिम एशिया (मध्य पूर्व) मे बढ़ैत संघर्ष के कारण गैस के आपूर्ति प्रभावित भेल, जाहि के कारण नेपाल तेल निगम के निदेशक मंडल 29 फरवरी के मात्र आधा सिलेंडर (7.1 किलो) गैस बेचब आ वितरण के निर्णय लेलक।

आधा सिलेंडर गैस बांटला स बेसी उपभोक्ता क रसोईघर कए कम मात्रा मे गैस स रोशन भ सकल। बाजार मे एक तरहक संतुलन बनल छल।

मुदा जेना-जेना गैस के आयात किछु आसान भेल, निगम 31 जुलाई सं सामान्य 14.2 किलोग्राम के फुल सिलेंडर गैस के वितरण फेर सं शुरू क देलक.पहिने जे उपभोक्ता के कमी के सामना करय पड़ल छल ओ पूरा सिलेंडर मिलैत देरी भारी संख्या मे गैस खरीदय लगलाह. उपभोक्ता अपन सबटा खाली सिलेंडर बाजार मे अनलक। हितधारक के कहनाय छनि जे आधा सिलेंडर के बाजार मे भेजला पर जे बैलेंस बनल छल ओ पूरा सिलेंडर के बिक्री शुरू होइते बाधित भ गेल, आओर अचानक गैस मिलनाय मुश्किल भ गेल.

नेपाल एलपी गैस उद्योग संघ के अध्यक्ष दीवान बहादुर चन्द के अनुसार अगिला दू-तीन दिन के भीतर उपभोक्ता के गैस आपूर्ति में किछु सहजता महसूस होयत, मुदा बाजार के पूर्ण रूप स सामान्य अवस्था में वापस आबय में एक महीना आओर लागत।

अध्यक्ष चांद के अनुसार भारत स गैस गोली के आगमन हाल में बढ़ल अछि। सोमदिन मात्र नेपाल मे करीब ११५ सँ १२५ गोली घुसल, मंगलदिन वीरगंज सीमा सँ ९० सँ ९५ गैस गोली गुजरि रहल अछि ।

अध्यक्ष चंद कहलनि जे, भारत के बरौनी रिफाइनरी मे रखरखाव के काज के कारण पहिने ओतय सं रोजाना मात्र 10-15 गाड़ी आबि रहल छल, मुदा सोमदिन ओतय सं 48 भरल गोली आयल छल, ओहि मे सं बेसी काठमांडू घाटी के लेल अछि, बरौनी सं लोड भेल गैस 3 दिन के भीतर बाजार मे पहुंचत।

एकरऽ अलावा भारत केरऽ पारादीप (ओडिशा) स॑ भी गैस आबी रहलऽ छै । मुदा ओतय सं नेपाल के दूरी करीब 1250 किलोमीटर अछि ताहि लेल लोडेड गैस उपभोक्ता तक पहुंचय मे 10 दिन तक के समय लगैत अछि. भारत के हल्दिया आ दुर्गापुर स गैस भले बंद भ गेल अछि, मुदा उद्योगपति क कहब अछि जे मथुरा स आपूर्ति मे किछु बढ़ोतरी भेल अछि।

बाजार के मांग पूरा करय लेल नेपाल तेल निगम आयात कोटा सेहो बढ़ा देलक अछि. पिछला मास 50 हजार मीट्रिक टन क कोटा एहि मास बढ़ा कए 55 हजार मीट्रिक टन भ गेल अछि। चांद के कहनाय छनि जे भले रोज करीब 130 सं 140 गाड़ी मे लोड भ रहल अछि मुदा बाजार तुरंत 100% सामान्य नहि भ जाएत.

ओ कहला जे पिछला दू मास मे करीब 30 हजार मीट्रिक टन गैस क आयात कम भेल, जाहि स बाजार प्रभावित भेल, आब ओहि सबटा खाली सिलेंडर कए फेर स भरबा मे बेसी समय लागत।

'गैस कोटा मे 15 प्रतिशत स बेसी क बढ़ोतरी'।

एखन बाजार मे गैस क कमी कम करबा लेल टेकू स्थित डिपो स नेपाल गैस, सुगम, एवरेस्ट, श्रीराम, सागर गैस, आ नमक व्यापार निगम (एसटीसी) क माध्यम स उपभोक्ता कए गैस वितरित करबाक व्यवस्था कैल गेल अछि।

नेपाल तेल निगमके प्रवक्ता मनोज ठाकुरके अनुसार टेकुसँ प्रतिदिन ८०० सँ १२५० सिलिण्डर बिका रहल अछि । हुनी जानकारी देलकै कि निगम नँ अपनौ नियमित कोटा स॑ अधिक गैस के आग्रह करलकै, आरू भारतीय पक्ष न॑ बतैलकै कि हुनी हर महीना ५५,००० मीट्रिक टन तलक के आपूर्ति करी सकै छै ।

सामान्य समय मे 48 हजार मीट्रिक टन गैस क खपत भेल। ठाकुर कहला जे अगर हम अपन आंकड़ा आ सीमा शुल्क विभाग क आंकड़ा देखब त जेतना गैस क खपत भ रहल अछि ओहि स बेसी गैस आयात भ रहल अछि, जे 10 स 15 प्रतिशत तक भ रहल अछि, रोज सौ स बेसी गोली गुजरैत अछि।

ओना वितरण मे किछु व्यावहारिक समस्या अछि। ओना त टेकू मे नाम आ नम्बर दर्ज करला के बाद गैस देल जाइत अछि, मुदा पता चलल अछि जे किछु लोक दिन मे दू-तीन बेर गैस लेबय लेल अबैत छथि, साइकिल पर ल क। असली उपभोक्ता क॑ कठिनाई के सामना करना पड़॑ छै, कैन्हेंकि एक ही घरऽ के बहुत लोग कतार म॑ खड़ा होय जाय छै आरू मजदूर गैस केरऽ कई सिलेंडर लेली जाय छै ।

काला विपणन मे लागल लोक कए सजा देल जाएत

गैस के सुचारू आपूर्ति के लेल जतय प्रयास भ रहल अछि ओतहि एहि कमी के फायदा उठा क ब्लैक मार्केटिंग सं जुड़ल लोक सेहो सक्रिय छथिन्ह. निगम कए शिकायत भेटल अछि जे एकटा गिरोह सक्रिय अछि, दिन मे अपन दोकान क शटर बंद क ‘गैस नहि’ कहैत अछि, आ राति मे चुपके स गैस बेसी दाम पर बेचैत अछि।

प्रवक्ता ठाकुर कहलनि जे, हम पुलिस के मदद सं एहन ब्लैक मार्केटर के नियंत्रित करब, हम पुलिस के तैनाती करब, छापामारी करब, आ उपभोक्ता के ई कहय के गलत प्रथा में लागल लोक के खिलाफ सख्त कार्रवाई करब, मुदा ओकरा गुप्त रूप सं भेजब।
